name: Nava Kailasam — the Nine Planetary Abodes of Shiva on the Tamiraparani
theme: Nine Shiva temples along the Tamiraparani, each held as a planetary shrine of the Navagraha, raised in tradition by Sage Agastya's disciple
region: Tamil Nadu (Tirunelveli & Thoothukudi, along the Tamiraparani)
description: The Nava Kailasam are nine temples of Shiva strung along the Tamiraparani in the far south, near Tirunelveli and Thoothukudi — the Shaiva companion to the Nava Tirupati that share the same river. By tradition Sage Agastya cast nine flowers upon the Tamiraparani and bade his disciple Uromacha Munivar raise a shrine of Kailasanathar wherever each came to rest, so that the nine are worshipped together as the planetary Kailasam, each linked to one of the Navagraha. Papanasam, where the river leaves the hills, is the Sun; Cheranmahadevi the Moon; Kodaganallur, Mars; Kunnathur, Rahu; Murappanadu, Jupiter; Srivaikuntam, Saturn; Thenthiruperai, Mercury; Rajapathy, Ketu; and Sendhapoomangalam, Venus, at the close near the sea. The villages lie strung along the Tamiraparani, and devotees take the nine in a single pilgrimage, seeking at each the grace of its planet.
